title: How package tracking works

segments.text: How does your phone know where your package is?
Usually, there's no tracker in the box. Just a barcode that gets scanned, again and again.
Step one: every parcel gets its own barcode. International mail even ends in two letters for the country that sent it.
Step two: at each sorting center, a scanner reads it and stores a tiny note: what happened, when, and where. Your app just lists those notes.
Step three, the surprise: between two scans, there's nothing new to show. That's why in transit can look stuck.
And the live location on the map? It comes from the driver's handheld scanner, at the very last step.
So your package isn't tracked live. It leaves a trail of scans.
Ever had one stuck in transit?

sources: https://upu.int/UPU/media/upu/files/postalSolutions/programmesAndServices/standards/S10-12.pdf (UPU S10: 13-character item identifier for individually tracked items incl. parcels: 2-letter service indicator, 8-digit serial number, check digit, 2-letter country code)

https://postalpro.usps.com/mnt/glusterfs/2024-01/Pub%20199_v29_01192024_0.pdf (USPS Publication 199 v29: 'The IMpb or unique tracking barcode is required for all parcels'; the scan event extract file 'contains tracking information about the movement of packages'; each event has Event Date, Event Time and Event ZIP; e.g. 'Your item arrived at our USPS facility in CITY, STATE ZIPCODE on DATE at TIME', 'Your item is out for delivery on DATE at TIME')

https://faq.usps.com/articles/FAQ/Where-is-my-package (USPS: 'USPS uses many package tracking status scans'; In Transit / Arrived / Departed USPS Facility scans 'may appear multiple times from the same facility and/or on different days'; 'Additional tracking information will display when the package arrives at unit and is out for delivery'; Out for Delivery: prepared at the local Post Office, delivered by a carrier today)

https://www.oversight.gov/sites/default/files/oig-reports/DR-AR-18-001.pdf (USPS OIG 2018: 'Carriers use a handheld Mobile Delivery Device (MDD) to scan and transmit package tracking data. MDDs use a cellular network and Global Positioning System (GPS) technology to obtain real-time delivery tracking and location information')
